analysis.investment_thesis: Rikhav Securities is a small-cap stockbroker riding the retail broking boom — revenue tripled to INR 328 Cr in 2025 but net profit fell to INR 24 Cr from INR 42 Cr and operating cash flow swung to -INR 188 Cr. Broking is a cyclical, commoditised business that sits outside my circle of competence; the cheap 6.6x P/E reflects earnings volatility, not value.
key_strengths: Low borrowings (INR 5 Cr vs equity of INR 244 Cr) — conservative balance sheet
Reported ROCE 16.7% and P/E 6.63 optically cheap
key_risks: Net profit fell 43% YoY (INR 42→24 Cr) despite revenue tripling — margin collapse
Operating CF negative in 3 of last 4 years (-188 Cr in 2025) — poor earnings quality
Broking is cyclical and commoditised; earnings tied to market volumes and retail euphoria
red_flags: Operating CF -INR 188 Cr in 2025 vs reported PAT of +INR 24 Cr — huge divergence
Profit declining while revenue explodes suggests unsustainable trading income or pricing pressure
Tiny INR 159 Cr market cap with FII/DII near zero — low institutional scrutiny
analysis.detailed_analysis:
This is not the kind of business I buy. Stockbroking earnings are tied to market cycles — volumes, IPO activity, F&O churn — and the last two years of Indian retail exuberance have inflated the entire sector. Rikhav's numbers tell the story: revenue 36→49→111→328 Cr, but net profit peaked at 42 Cr in FY24 and has already dropped to 24 Cr in FY25. Operating cash flow of -INR 188 Cr against a reported PAT of +INR 24 Cr is a massive red flag; in broking this usually reflects client funding/margin book swings, but it means accounting profit is not cash. I want predictable consumer demand, not market-linked earnings.

The balance sheet is clean (debt of just INR 5 Cr, equity of INR 244 Cr after what looks like a fresh equity raise) and promoter holding at 64% is acceptable — those are the only positives. But ROE of 12.9% is below my 15% floor, there is no dividend history visible, and the business has no moat against bigger discount brokers like Zerodha, Groww, or Angel One. The optically low P/E of 6.6x is a classic cyclical trap: cheap on peak earnings that are already rolling over. I would leave this alone and wait for a quality consumer or financial compounder at a fair price.
